FIGURE FOR THIS SLIDE (frozen before parallel authoring; the decision is made, do not re-argue it):
- archetype: hierarchy — a tree of boxes with connectors from parent to children.
- takeaway (the figure's headline, verbatim): "검증 후 개통한다"
- nodes, in this order, labels VERBATIM (never reword, add or drop one):
  1. label="단계1" desc="설명 문구 1" before="4.6%" after="2.2%" figure="12%"
  2. label="단계2" desc="설명 문구 2" before="5.6%" after="3.2%" figure="13%"
  3. label="단계3" desc="설명 문구 3" before="6.6%" after="4.2%" figure="14%" (EMPHASIS)
  4. label="단계4" desc="설명 문구 4" before="7.6%" after="5.2%" figure="15%"
  5. label="단계5" desc="설명 문구 5" before="8.6%" after="6.2%" figure="16%"
- density: high — each node carries its label, its supporting phrase and its figure.
- Single out the node marked EMPHASIS: filled with the primary colour or accent-outlined, and echo it in the headline.
- This is one of the deck's HERO pages: the figure IS the page. Give it the whole canvas between the header and the bottom content line, with the takeaway as the only headline and no bullet list beside it.
- Where this brief and the VISUAL STORY PLAN disagree on the figure's shape, this brief wins. The figure itself is drawn by the archetype component library under the contract below; the server rejects a slide that departs from it.
FIGURE CONTRACT (the figure below is finished markup; reproduce it, do not redesign it):
1. Paste the following figure into the slide body EXACTLY as given — every element, class, data-qid, data-native, data-qid-ignore and text — at the place your layout reserves for it. Give its container an explicit width and height in px, computed for THIS page rather than chosen from habit: the width is your full content width, and the height is 648 minus the container's own top. The container takes the whole content area under the header, and its bottom edge lands ON y=648px — this deck's bottom content line — not somewhere above it. A container that stops short of that line leaves a blank band across the foot of the slide, and that band is a defect rather than restraint: it is the most common failure on figure pages. Measured on real slides, the median figure box stopped 76px above the line and the figure's own lowest text 108px above it. Never make the box shorter than 430px, and never fill a shortfall with an empty spacer, an invented caption, or a taller gap above the figure. The figure fills that box: size and place the container you wrap it in, and put no width, height, margin or position on the figure's own root element — the library sizes the root to 100% of its container, so a margin on the root pushes the figure past the canvas edge.
2. The figure's stylesheet is injected by the server. Do NOT write CSS for any .ig* class, do NOT add a class the library does not define, and do NOT put a style attribute or a <style> element inside the figure (the only exception: left/top on .ig-co / .ig-pin, kept in the percentages the skeleton gives, and the px size of a scene img).
3. You MAY: swap any icon inside an .ig-ic for another from the ICON MENU; rewrite the UPPERCASE placeholder words in the deck language; and do what the ARCHETYPE NOTE allows. Every other text is verbatim from the plan — never reword, translate, add or drop a label.
4. Everything outside the figure (header, eyebrow, page number, any supporting text) is yours to author under the design system as usual, but no other diagram, card grid or chart may compete with the figure.
ARCHETYPE NOTE (hierarchy): The first planned node is the root; every other node is a child under the bar.
